videos.script: A typo in a spreadsheet does not look like a typo. It looks like data. {{typo}} Type Online with a space after it, and nothing complains. The sale is there. But a total by channel no longer finds it, and the three channels stop adding up to the whole. {{totals}} Data validation is a rule that sits on a cell and checks what is typed into it. A whole number from one to fifty. A date that is not in the future. A sale code nobody has used. {{rules}} The best rule is a drop-down. Nobody mistypes a word they pick from a list. And when the list reads from a table, a new product appears in it on its own. {{dropdown}} A rule can also talk. It can say what the cell wants before you type. And it decides what happens after. Refuse, warn, or only inform. {{messages}} Then the honest part. Validation checks typing, and only typing. A paste walks straight past it. So the lesson ends with the command that finds what got through. {{circles}} By the end you have a sheet called New sales. The next sale can be typed there, and it is hard to type wrong.
